I'm a mod on /r/firearms.

What is the average day of a mod like?

I wake up, eat food, browse the internet, go to work, come home, and browse some more. On the weekends I spend time with my beautiful and amazing girlfriend.

How much time do you spend and what sort of issues do you deal with?

I am usually logged in on my phone, so I get notifications whenever I get modmail or a PM. I also utilize automoderator to send me a PM if a thread gets more than 2 reports, or if a certain topic is discussed (mainly so I can some and read the discussion because I'm interested!). I mostly look at the links that are posted, and check the account overview of the user that posted the link. It's easy to spot a spammer, and it's easy to ban them. Usually I just delete their thread, send them a PM with definitions of spam, tell them how they can post their content without spamming, and wish them a nice day. If they don't comply, I ban them. Trolls are the same way. If I see someone acting inflammatory, I check their account. If all they do is insult and troll people, I ban them. Aside from that, this is all I really deal with. I only have to delete threads maybe three or four times a month. I've banned less than 20 people in 3 years.

Do you need to be available 24 hours a day?

No, but I get notifications. I do have to sleep and work, and sometimes I'm busy with my life. Most of the time I can deal with things instantly from my phone, but sometimes I'll only notice hours or a day later when I get back to my PC.

Do you have to read every submission and comment?

No, but I'm not just a moderator, I'm a user as well... So I usually do read every submission and comment that goes through the subreddit I moderate anyways.

Can you do what you need to do from your phone?

Yes, absolutely. I use RedditIsFun platinum, and my Chrome mobile browser.

How do you find additional mods?

I don't trust other people to not abuse their power, so I will not bring on new moderators. I can only trust myself.

Considering that Voat is currently a tiny community, being a mod is no different than being a regular user. I mod /v/roguelikes and the current challenge is getting the community up to a point where I don't have to constantly post to keep things going.
